title: Protection and Assistance Measures for Delivery Riders
what_it_is: Protection and Assistance Measures for Delivery Riders

sections.label: Self-employed and platform workers numbers
sections.summary: In 2020, about 190,000 persons were mainly self-employed, of whom about 79,000 worked with matching platform companies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In 2020, about 190,000 persons were engaged in self-employment as their main source of income, of which about 79,000 worked with matching platform companies.

sections.label: Median income of three occupations
sections.summary: From 2018 to 2020, median monthly income of full-time employed residents in these three occupations ranged between $1,500 and $2,000.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: From 2018 to 2020, the median monthly income of full-time employed residents in these three occupations ranged between $1,500 and $2,000.

sections.label: Advisory Committee for platform workers
sections.summary: An Advisory Committee will be convened to strengthen protections for platform workers and ensure a more balanced relationship between platforms and workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To look into strengthening protections for platform workers, specifically delivery workers, private-hire car drivers and taxi drivers, and ensuring a more balanced relationship between platforms and platform workers, an Advisory Committee will be convened.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The committee will need time to consult widely with stakeholders and study these issues carefully before making its recommendations.

sections.label: Reporting gig worker injuries
sections.summary: MOM is asked whether it will consider requiring gig platforms to report injuries when workers are injured during gig economy work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: First, Mr Speaker, can MOM share whether MOM will consider requiring the gig platforms to report instances of injuries, when the worker is injured in the course of their gig economy work?

sections.label: Compensation for deceased workers' families
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked whether it has information on compensation and support provided to families of workers who lost their lives.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Does the Ministry have information on what compensation and support were provided to the families of these workers, who lost their lives?

sections.label: Fatality compensation for gig workers
sections.summary: The speaker lacks information on fatality compensation, noting gig workers are not treated as employees and compensation would likely not match employees' under the Employment Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: On the second question, of those cases of fatality as a result of gig work, whether they do enjoy the same level of compensation, I am afraid I do not have information for that.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Suffice to say that, today, they are not treated as employees.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, I would imagine the amount of compensation, if there is, would not be commensurate with what employees would probably get under the Employment Act as well.
